text:
LAK arrives at NYI on a high note after a long skid. The Kings came back from two goals down to beat WSH 5-2 on Tuesday, snapping a six-game winless run (0-4-2), and Darcy Kuemper saved 2.7 goals more than the shots deserved. Even so, they're 1-3-1 in their last five and are without Alex Turcotte. This is game two of a five-game road trip. NYI beat ANA 3-2 at home Tuesday and is 3-1-1 in its last five, but Calum Ritchie and Matias Maccelli are both out. With Maccelli gone, Simon Holmstrom has moved onto the first power-play unit and is up to 20:11 a night from 15:43. Kyle Palmieri is up to 19:14 from 15:38.

The numbers say these teams are close. At five on five, LAK has taken 49% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and NYI 53%. The model has tonight at 2.89 expected goals for NYI and 2.87 for LAK. The goalie matchup is the clearest gap. Projected starter Ilya Sorokin is at +8.8 goals saved above expected this season and +22.3 last year, while Kuemper is at -2.6 and -6.8. LAK also takes 4.6 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays.

For LAK, watch Adrian Kempe (37% to score, top power-play option) and Artemi Panarin (33% to score, 70% to get a point, flagged as due). For NYI, Bo Horvat is at 41% to score and 69% to get a point, with Palmieri at 24%.
